long_biography.plain_text:
Ezratti moved from Israel to Washington, D.C., in 1974 and worked as a bank teller before relocating to Florida. Two years later, he and his father-in-law, engineer Joseph Hanin, formed GL Homes around a single duplex in Hollywood. The private builder expanded steadily, then accelerated after Hurricane Andrew as displaced demand shifted north and its land options supported hundreds of sales.

GL Homes remained focused on large master-planned Florida communities, including developments for buyers aged 55 and over, rather than pursuing a national footprint. Ezratti handed the presidency to Misha in 2016 and continues as chairman, separating founder stewardship from daily operating leadership. The company now ranks among America's largest private homebuilders, while the family retains control.
